answer_1.quote: Opinion summarization aims to tackle this problem by generating a concise summary of the reviews... Rationale-based opinion summarization outputs representative opinions summarizing the reviews as well as one or more rationales.
answer_1.outputs: Extractive summaries consisting of representative opinions (e.g., "location is great") and associated rationales (supporting review sentences).

answer_2.quote: We use the following four automatic measures for evaluating rationales for a given opinion... To measure relatedness... To measure specificity... To measure popularity... To measure diversity... We also evaluate rationale candidate sets with Silhouette scores, coherence (TF‑IDF based), and entailment score (SummaC).

answer_4.quote: We ask annotators to compare the two types of summaries in a pairwise manner based on four criteria: which summary includes more information (informativeness), which summary contains less repeated phrases (non‑redundancy), which summary is easier to read (coherence), and which summary is more useful for decision making (usefulness)... For rationales we ask annotators to compare the two rationale sets ... based on three properties: relatedness, specificity, and diversity.
answer_4.guideline: Pairwise comparison of generated summaries or rationale sets according to the listed criteria.
